event_overview.title: About Ukraine Negotiations
event_overview.subject: Ukraine Negotiations
event_overview.summary: Ukraine negotiations are the evolving diplomatic efforts to end Russia’s full-scale war against Ukraine, which began on February 24, 2022. They are not a single permanent conference or treaty process: direct Ukrainian-Russian contacts, U.S.-led efforts, European coordination, ceasefire proposals, humanitarian measures, security guarantees and longer-term settlement issues can proceed through different channels.

facts.label: Conflict context
facts.value: The negotiations concern the war following Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022; the UN has continued to frame a settlement around the sovereignty, independence and territorial integrity of Ukraine within its internationally recognized borders.

facts.label: Format
facts.value: There is no single standing negotiation venue or universally agreed peace text. European coalition leaders have supported direct dialogue between Ukraine and Russia with active U.S. and European participation, beginning with a ceasefire and followed by wider negotiations.

facts.label: Core participation principle
facts.value: European positions have stated that any peace agreement should be negotiated with Ukraine’s full and continuous participation; matters affecting the EU or NATO require the consent of their respective members and allies.

facts.label: European coordination
facts.value: A major vehicle for European and partner coordination is the Coalition of the Willing, established in March 2025 at the initiative of the United Kingdom and France. As of November 3, 2026, the UK Ministry of Defence described it as bringing together 35 nations to support Ukraine and press Russia economically and diplomatically.

facts.label: Stated settlement objectives
facts.value: European and UN statements have emphasized an immediate, full and unconditional ceasefire; a peace consistent with the UN Charter and international law; and security arrangements intended to deter renewed aggression. European planning has also contemplated a multinational force only at Ukraine’s invitation and after hostilities end and other conditions are met.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline tracks the specific development involving a European diplomatic team for upcoming talks, rather than every negotiating channel, military development, humanitarian exchange, sanction decision or Ukraine-related diplomatic initiative.

highlights.summary: Iran has claimed responsibility for targeting a US radar system in Bahrain, asserting that the system was destroyed. The situation remains tense, with ongoing clashes in the Strait of Hormuz.

The US military denies the radar was destroyed and reports intercepting two drones.

event_overview.title: About Iran War
event_overview.subject: Iran War
event_overview.summary: The Iran War refers here to the 2026 armed conflict between the United States and Iran, including U.S. military operations in and against Iran and maritime-security operations around the Strait of Hormuz. The conflict has combined direct military action, disputes over commercial navigation through the strait, and U.S. congressional debate over the President’s authority to continue hostilities.

facts.label: Start of U.S. operation
facts.value: U.S. Central Command says it began Operation Epic Fury against Iran on February 28, 2026, at the President’s direction.

facts.label: Geographic focus
facts.value: The Strait of Hormuz, connecting the Gulf of Oman and the Persian Gulf, has been a central operational area; CENTCOM described it as an international sea passage and a key trade corridor while conducting mine-clearance and shipping-security operations.

facts.label: Stated U.S. military objectives
facts.value: The White House said the February 28 operation was directed at Iran’s ballistic-missile and drone capabilities, navy, and defense-industrial base; these are stated U.S. objectives, not an independent assessment of the conflict’s effects.

facts.label: Maritime escalation
facts.value: CENTCOM said U.S. strikes beginning July 7 followed attacks on neutral-flagged commercial vessels transiting the Strait of Hormuz on July 6–7, with targets including missile sites, air defenses, maritime assets, support infrastructure, and command-and-control capabilities.

facts.label: U.S. war-powers framework
facts.value: Under the War Powers Resolution, the President generally must terminate a reported use of U.S. armed forces within 60 days unless Congress declares war, specifically authorizes the use, extends the period by law, or cannot meet because of an armed attack; the statute also describes removal when Congress directs it by concurrent resolution.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline covers a narrow set of late-July 2026 escalatory, congressional, energy-market, Houthi, and ceasefire-related developments; it does not provide a complete account of the war’s origins, all military operations, humanitarian consequences, diplomacy, or legal disputes.
